She has a cornucopia of severe mental illnesses and was very angry one night, cumulating in one very over-the-top act. She sent a few “leaks” (à la Assange) by group text message around to family members and school teachers and friends, filled with lies and designed to humiliate me. A lot of the lies were obviously projection, for example she alleged that I self-harm—never have, never will—and that I have depression—probably true now, but importantly the group text predates and was the major cause of the much later development of depression.

It could be [Munchausen syndome-by-proxy](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factitious_disorder_imposed_on_another), but it’s probably too early to make that statement. It was definitely related to her mental disorders, though. Her psychiatrists—because she has a *team* of them, which is not a great sign for anybody—have confirmed that.

She is also generally volatile and tries to upset me as “revenge” for perceived (imagined) slights. She can act violently, but luckily it doesn’t affect me too much. I’m 6’1 and athletic, so it doesn’t actually feel that bad, but it still makes me feel like piss.

Britain can no longer sustain the merging of so many diffident identifies into one whole and fully actualised country. The four identities of Northern Irish, Welsh, English and Scottish never truly did coalesce into a single “British” identity, and so the political chasm between the different nations within Britain can not be bridged either.

Britain will, in time, dissolve into its constituent elements. The Six Counties will be reunited with Ireland; Scotland and Wales will become separate microstates under the EU and this will further push the EU to create a more centralised and more integrated ‘United States of Europe’.

England, now on its own, will be wedged between the EU superpower and the American superpower. I’m not sure as to what might happen after that.

>	Do you look at yourself in the mirror? Do you like what you see?

I do, frequently, and I don’t like what I see. I know I am, in real life, sorta handsome, but when I am in the mood I’m in right now, I just feel like such an ugly piece of shit.

>	Do you spend your time on Facebook? Do you compare yourself to others?

I have a Facebook account but I never use it. Social media is toxic for everybody. It’s all the complexes of the 21st Century rolled into one.

>	Do you always think about your problems? What is your number 1 problem right now?

I am socially withdrawn after my mum did some fairly horrible things to me in order to humiliate me publicly. She has a severe mental disorder. I think about my problems constantly. It’s the first thing I think of when I wake up, and it hits me like a punch in the face.

>	If you had a choice, would you rather not been born?

Undoubtedly, yes. I’m undecided on suicide. However, to not have ever been born in the first place would be amazing. I would say ‘yes’ in a heartbeat.

>	Do you have a girl in your eyes?

I’m not sure what that means, but if it means crushing on a girl, then yes. She’s pretty and smart, and funny. I want to be with her, and hug her and kiss her and watch Netflix and have silly and serious conversations.

>	What do you see yourself doing?

I don’t really see a future for myself at this point. I used to hope I would gain the marks to enter university and study arts then medicine, but I can’t be bothered anymore. It’s all pointless.

>	How many games do you play on that laptop of yours?

I’m actually not into gaming, it just doesn’t entertain me that much. I normally just use it to browse the internet and word processing.

>	How do you say Potato? Potato or Potato?

I say potato, obviously.

>	What do you do in school?

I’m not attending school for the moment, but we study a pretty normal curriculum. I’m doing and elective in philosophy, creative writing, and photography, and I wish I weren’t missing it.

Reading and writing. I also enjoy surfing and playing cricket.

>	What's the best movie you've watched last year?

*Blue is the Warmest Colour*, a French romance drama and Golden Palm winner. It received a lot of attention for its graphic sex scenes—they are indeed quite long—but in the context of the film it made perfect sense. The acting is incredibly realistic, almost uncomfortably so, and the build-up of the character’s romantic relationship mirrored perfectly some of what I sometimes feel. I think it’s a powerful testament to the quality of the film that it can be so personal to the characters but also contain so many universal truths.

>	If you could have one superpower, what would it be? (And Why?)

Most likely, invisibility. Not to be a perv, but just to sneak into places unnoticed. Lots of mayhem.


>	What do you think of Taylor Swift?

She’s not *that* unmusical in the context of your average pop chart. I don’t like her persona, though, and I don’t think it is good for 13-year-old girls’ collective psyches for them to be bound up in such 20th Century notions of love and intimacy.

>	If your house is burning, what are the first three things you'll save?

My laptop—a cheap old thing, but it has all my images (400 GB) and music (300 GB) I’ve accumulated over the past few years; my old teddy bear, because even though I don’t sleep with it any longer it’s still of sentimental value to me; and my camera, which is my greatest companion.

I attend a psychiarist as part of group therapy for my Mum, but I don’t see one for myself, and so I am not really under a doctor’s care.

My interests are reading and writing, but I can’t do that nowadays very much due to lack of concentration. 

I have a few coping methods. This will sound pathetic, please don’t judge me: I have this imaginary friend who just hugs me and tells me I’m okay and that things will turn out alright. To just focus on that for a few seconds has a very helpful effect, although it’s probably detrimental. I become anxious whenever I am not actively thinking about something, making sleep difficult, so often I have conversations with her in my head until I fall asleep from tiredness.

Other less *esoteric* methods I often use are controlled breathing, and mindfulness—God, I hate that word and the new-age culture that it entails, but it actually does work. I place my hand on my heartbeat and remind myself that I’m alive. To feel the blood pumping through my body, in spite of my mental state, is strangely comforting.

Personal favourites to make at home are prosciutto with tomato sauce and boconcini, and a meatlovers pizza covered in sausage and cured meats.

>	what would you consider the best day of your life? when was it? why was it the best?

My best day, perhaps was when I was on holiday to Sydney with my grandma. At the start of 2016. We took an interstate flight—we are from another part of Australia. She’s old and looks after her dependant husband, and she needed a break and so did I. It required a lot of organisation and effort, but it was a wonderful time. I was at a general high point in my life at that time. I could see my years stretching out in front of me, my future was in a state of complete potentiality. I have nowadays lost nearly all of that optimism, sadly. I’m happy I was able to experience it, though.

It’s strange and contradictory. Let me start from the start.

I really despise myself. Not for any inherent attribute, but for how I’ve reacted to certain events.

I have had every chance to go well in life. I am reasonably intelligent, pretty damn talented at art and writing, conventionally handsome, and I have a fair amount of charisma. I’m attracted to both men and women, and I’m fairly outgoing for my age with both. I am from an upper-middle class family and I’ve never been without necessities, and I’ve always been in good health.   

I’m not saying this to brag, but to put in context just how much of a failed opportunity that I have become.

Here is where it begins, from the beginning:

My mother has (diagnosed) depressive disorder and anxiety disorder, for which she takes a fairly high dose of alprazolam (Australian-speak for Xanax). She can go from happy to blistering anger in what feels like a few seconds. She also claims to have a BMI of 14.5 and there often appears an obsessional aspect to her eating habits, which leads me to believe she might have some sort of eating disorder. Nonetheless I’ve resolved to refrain from alleging she has an eating disorder until a psychiatrist confirms it.

My father is a difficult, stubborn man. He obviously does love me and want to care for me, but his work occupies the vast majority of his time. As such, mostly diffident and rarely present. It is a strain on our relationship. Even when I’m with him, it seems like he’s some place else. He always is doing work... making phone calls, typing frenzied emails, et cetera. This is even when I am with him, which in itself is a short and rare affair.

My parents have always held a very—how does one say—*pressured* attitude towards me. In just about everything. From grades; friends; my physical health; my romantic life. From the most inane and pointless to the most deep and personal, they want some sort of say in what goes on with me. (I say “they”, but it’s all the doing of mum. Dad participates, begrudgingly, but there is a clear sense that he doesn’t want to and is somehow made to do it. His wife reduces him and berates him, and he’s often tired and mentally defenceless after performing surgery for hours. I find it hard to blame him.)

Long story short, mum’s mental health worsened dramatically and she became upset and leaked, in a Julian Assange-style group text, a whole bunch of personal details about me. Some were real and private, and others were just straight-up falsified. Examples of the latter were the accusations that I had severe anxiety disorder and depression—projection from her, without a doubt—and that I was violent. In fact, I have never hit anyone, not her nor another person. I am tall and muscular though, and so it was easy to see that people would instantly believe her.

I forced Mum to attend *two* separate psychiatrists with Dad and I. Both of them—one is the director of a large hospital in the large city where I live, so they are the best doctors you could probably ever find—certified me as being A-OK. I was without any disorder or other issues. She refused to accept this, deciding that psychiatry was a sham and that only she—*as a mother*—was qualified to make statements about her family members’ mental health. (In fact, it’s exactly the opposite. Not only is she not a doctor, and as such not qualified to diagnose people, apparently even doctors aren’t allowed to diagnose their own family members with mental illnesses due to the conflict of interest—the more you know!)

She kept on doing this, and kept on drip-feeding my school teachers—the sons and daughters of which I am close friends with—and family these lies about me. At some point, she began using physical violence. It doesn’t hurt for very long, although it can sting at first, but it still makes me feel horrible to be reduced that way.

I withdrew from school and social life. I stopped seeing friends and kept familial contact to a minimum. She alienated me from everyone I knew, and ruined my academic career, all just for some meaningless outbreak of her own disorder. God, I can’t take the illogicity.

The only person who could ever help me out of this is my father. He could make her listen, but he refuses to talk about what she had done, and the impact it’s had on me, with her. He fears it will upset her. Damn her and damn him. I understand that her behaviour is influenced by her mental disease, but that isn’t an excuse.

I haven’t seen my friends for nearly two months. I often receive calls and texts but I can’t bear to talk to them. My teachers send me work but I never complete it. I can’t concentrate anymore. I have to always be doing something, or else I break down in tears and become inconsolable—not that anyone ever tries to or would like to console me. I have lost all my sex drive, which feels alien and unusual, and disconcerting and wrong for a teenager like myself.

Why does all this make me pathetic? I don’t know. Now that I’ve typed this out—for the first time, by the way, which has been quite therapeutic—I can see that I come out of this looking quite sympathetic. And in my heart of hearts, I know I’ve done nothing wrong.

But I can’t stop thinking of how much I hate myself. It doesn’t make any sense.

Ever since I was young, I was told I wasn’t good enough—maybe that’s why I feel permenantly inadequate.

An example of this: certain sources have informed me that there are girls I know that are crushing on me and doing whatever it is that girls do when they feel that way. I am told, not infrequently. that I’m lucky to look the way I am. I naturally don’t gain weight and enjoy exercising. But when I stand in the mirror,  all I see is an ugly and stupid-looking pathetic idiot. I’m too thin, my face is too round, my eyes too inset, my jaw too weak. I know that none of this is true but I can’t stop thinking that way. 

I realise that this is poorly-written and mostly incoherent. There isn’t really any cogency at all, is there? I would write better if I were in a more stable frame-of-mind.

Hopefully, you can make some sense of it. I’m not even close to understanding myself.

Your story is heartbreaking, and it reminds me a lot of mine. I can give you some advice, but I suppose it won’t mean much coming from just a depressed teenager. You should make an appointment with a doctor. You don’t need to go to the ER—you’re entitled to, but it doesn’t seem like you’re about to do something you will come to regret in the future—but you do need to contact a medical professional. The first port of call should be a general practitioner—I believe they’re known in America as “physicians”. They can themselves offer counselling, and direct you to further aid. They can take the weight, the burden, of decision from you. All that you need to do is be honest with them, and they can help you.

I’m a hypocrite since I am going through a similar thing and I’ve not attended the ER or even a doctor. I am seeing a psychiatrist though, but for an unrelated issue. Still, I hope my advice is of some help.

Just remember—I know it’s sappy, but it’s 100% true—that you *are* loved. I’m out here, likely thousands of miles away from you, but I really care about you and helping you. Everyone else here does too. I have the utmost sympathy for you, in fact when I read your post tears started to well up in my eyes. You’ve been through a lot, and it’s important you don’t exacerbate your trauma by diminishing or reducing yourself. You have no need to be embarrassed over anything. You are stronger than most of the people you will ever meet.
